mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision point reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS changes (p > 0.05 in OLS regression).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS in the prior month correlates with stronger consumer confidence and corporate hiring intentions, which anticipate higher future profits and lift S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Payroll momentum does not predict SPX 20-day returns after controlling for CPI and S&P 500 option skew (R-squared < 0.01, p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (GDPC1) followed by a rebound above the prior quarter's level indicates a turning point in supply-side constraints, which accelerates aggregate demand and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls below prior quarter then rebounds above
failure_condition: No significant correlation between GDPC1 turning points and SPX 5-day returns (t-test p = 0.22).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly index of manufacturing production (INDPRO) exceeds its 12-month moving average by at least 2 percentage points, it reflects a sustained acceleration in supply capacity, which reduces cost pressures and supports higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO acceleration is not predictive of SPX returns after accounting for FEDFUNDS and CPI (multivariate R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 0.2% suggest the Federal Reserve is committed to monetary tightening, which raises real interest rates and dampens equity valuation multiples, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 0.2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns show positive sensitivity to CPIAUCSL declines (coefficient > 0, p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) followed by a sustained drop indicates a labor market correction that reduces optimism about future wage growth and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS peaks then declines for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: PAYEMS spikes do not precede SPX declines in a statistically significant way (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both industrial production (GDPC1) and consumer confidence (implied via HOUST) signal dual headwinds that suppress both supply and demand, amplifying the negative impact on equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Interaction term between GDPC1 and HOUST is not significant in explaining SPX 20-day returns (p > 0.05 in interaction regression).

mechanism_narrative: During a prolonged period of falling unemployment and rising consumer spending (implied by PAYEMS and HOUST trends), the S&P 500 exhibits higher forward returns due to regime-specific optimism about economic resilience, which is absent in contractionary regimes.
failure_condition: In contractionary regimes (e.g., rising unemployment, falling HOUST), the same proxies do not predict positive SPX 20-day returns (p > 0.05 in regime-split OLS).
